page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance belonging to the ecs.se1ne family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance profile characterized by average multi-core capabilities and weaker single-core execution. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively, reflecting the lower clock speed of the older Intel Xeon architecture. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, achieve average ratings within the middle 50% of tested instances. Memory bandwidth tests also demonstrate average performance, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 654.2 GB/sec and uncached large block writes at 53.85 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is its modest single-threaded performance, as evidenced by poor gzip compression and weak bzip3 decompression results. This makes it less suitable for single-threaded processing tasks. However, its high memory density provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-frequency compute. The instance is well-suited for database operations, as shown by average Passmark database and Redis SET performance, as well as static web serving, software compilation, and light LLM inference tasks.
